newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Chess-Upsets continue in World Cities Chess.
newsitem.headline: Chess-Upsets continue in World Cities Chess.

text.p: A startling loss by top seeds Moscow in the second round of the inaugural World Cities Chess Championship in Jakarta on Wednesday has left the title race wide open.

The all-Grandmaster Moscow team lost to unfancied Mandaluyung, with Filipino youngster Ronald Bancod scoring a sensational victory over former world title candidate Sergei Tiviakov in four hours and almost 100 moves.
Mandaluyung was joined in the lead by the capable Vietnamese team from Ho Chi Minh City and a rank outsider, Depok Kelapa, who upset their countrymen from Jakarta.
Sydney also moved up to within half a point of the lead with their second consecutive match win.
Of the European teams, only Oslo and Donetsk are close to the pace, the former after a controversial 2-2 draw with Depok Beji.
Oslo missed a chance to take clear first place when their top player Einar Gausel lost to fellow Grandmaster Herman Suradiradja.
Gausel's game became a source of dispute when an arbiter stepped in and stopped the players' chess clock when both Gausel and Suradiradja had less than 30 seconds to complete the game.

All the time Gausel was vigourously complaining that Suradiradja was moving a pawn around the board as if it was a powerful queen - the pawn having reached the eighth rank but not been replaced with a queen as the rules require.
Gausel was awarded a time penalty but this was insufficient for him to save the game in the face of his opponent's two queens.
To the delight of the partisan crowd surrounding the board, local hero Suradiradja checkmated Gausel with six seconds remaining on his clock.
The World Cities Championship continues until July 14.
